title: CSG Boolean Operations Editor
prompt:
Use Three.js to implement a real-time CSG (Constructive Solid Geometry) Boolean operations editor that supports union, subtraction, and intersection operations with real-time previews. Refer to the official three.js example webgl_geometry_csg, but modify it substantially.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following importmap in <head>, and import via ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
import { CSG } from 'three/addons/math/CSG.js';
// If the CSG module path is incorrect, Evaluator/Brush from three-bvh-csg may be used
// The following alternatives may also be used (choose one of the three options that can be imported successfully):
// import { SUBTRACTION, ADDITION, INTERSECTION, Evaluator, Brush } from 'three/addons/math/CSG.js';
</script>

Note: In Three.js r170, CSG functionality is located under the examples/jsm/ directory. You may implement CSG using any of the following methods:
- Method A: three/addons/math/CSG.js (if it exists)
- Method B: Implement a simplified CSG solution yourself (based on a BSP tree or another method)
- Method C: Use the three-bvh-csg library (add it through the CDN importmap)
Regardless of the method used, all three Boolean operations, union, subtract, and intersect, must execute correctly.

[Initial Geometries]
(1) Start with 2 primitives:
  - A sphere (SphereGeometry, radius=1.5) positioned at (0, 0, 0), color #4488ff
  - A cube (BoxGeometry, 2×2×2) positioned at (1, 0, 0), color #ff8844 (partially overlapping the sphere)
(2) Each primitive has a translucent wireframe showing its original shape (wireframe overlay, opacity=0.3).

[Boolean Operations]
(3) id="operation": A dropdown selector with values "union", "subtract", and "intersect". The default is "union".
(4) After switching the operation type, immediately recompute the CSG result and update the result mesh.
(5) The result mesh uses MeshStandardMaterial (metalness=0.2, roughness=0.5, color #88cc88).

[Adding Primitives]
(6) id="addPrimitive": A button that adds a new primitive when clicked.
(7) New primitive types cycle as follows: sphere → box → cylinder → sphere → ... (cycle in click order).
(8) The initial position of a new primitive is (primitiveCount * 0.8, 0, 0) (offset along the X axis to avoid complete overlap).
(9) Default dimensions for new primitives: sphere radius=1.2, box 1.8×1.8×1.8, cylinder(radiusTop=1, radiusBottom=1, height=2).

[Selecting and Transforming Primitives]
(10) Select a primitive by clicking its wireframe in the scene or through the list on the left (id="primitiveList").
(11) After selection, display 3 position sliders:
  - id="posX": range, min=-5, max=5, step=0.1
  - id="posY": range, min=-5, max=5, step=0.1
  - id="posZ": range, min=-5, max=5, step=0.1
(12) When a slider changes, update the primitive's position and recompute the CSG result.

[Result Mesh Information]
(13) id="vertexCount": The number of vertices in the result mesh.
(14) id="faceCount": The number of faces in the result mesh (number of triangles, i.e., index.count / 3 or geometry.attributes.position.count / 3).

[Lighting and Scene]
- A white DirectionalLight with intensity 1.0 positioned at (5, 8, 5).
- AmbientLight with intensity 0.4.
- GridHelper ground plane.
- OrbitControls.

[State Exposure (Required, Update After Operations)]
window.__3D_STATE__ = {
  primitiveCount: number,         // Number of primitives
  operation: string,              // "union" | "subtract" | "intersect"
  vertexCount: number,            // Number of vertices in the result mesh
  faceCount: number,              // Number of triangular faces in the result mesh
  primitives: [{                  // Information for each primitive
    type: string,                 // "sphere" | "box" | "cylinder"
    x: number, y: number, z: number,
    scaleX: number, scaleY: number, scaleZ: number
  }, ...]
}

Output a single standalone HTML file that can run when opened directly in a browser.
